metadata.definition: Homicide + rape + robbery + aggravated assault + electronic theft. Electronic robbery is a subset of robbery, not an additional category.
metadata.tripDefinition: Sum of monthly origin-destination Total Trips grand totals. These are trips, not unique riders.
metadata.reportingBreakExplanation: UCR before January 2025; NIBRS from January 2025. Offense counts across the break are not directly comparable.
limitations: Reconstructed series: not the unpublished table behind the news graphic. Original rates and retrospective graphics differ from category counts.
Seven quarters use bar heights rounded to integer counts; retain digitized-bars flags as estimates.
Uses report vintages identified on each row, including revisions of earlier quarters.
Some source PDFs contain raster graphics; the FY24 Q1 file is a PowerPoint archive despite its PDF extension.

FY19 four-category counts use retrospective monthly YTD snapshots and subtraction; corrections to earlier months can affect reconstructed quarters. Theft counts use exact printed monthly snatching labels, excluding force/fear robberies. The police reports warn their database figures are unaudited and may differ from official UCR totals.
FY19 Q2 uses revised 2018 robbery totals; FY19 Q3 uses revised January–March 2019 homicide and rape totals. Row-level arithmetic, contributing reports, and vintage caveats are retained.
The July 2019 source boundary is shown as a gap and dashed marker. It is distinct from the established January 2025 UCR/NIBRS methodology break.
metadata.sourceBreakExplanation: Monthly police/TriTech reconstruction through FY19; retrospective QPR category tables from FY20. Overlapping counts differ by source vintage. This is not an established offense-definition change.

publishedMetricDefinitionChange.explanation: FY21 Q1 lists four crimes against persons; FY21 Q2 adds electronic theft. This reconstruction uses the same five categories before and after, so the published aggregate expansion is not a category break in this series.
